```{r}
#does not work bc we did not give it arguments 
# this is the conversion formula 
temp_C <- (temp_F - 32) * 5 / 9
```


```{r}
#create fxn structure 
f_to_celsius <- function() {
  # code goes here
}

#add formula
f_to_celsius <- function() {
  temp_C <- (temp_F - 32) * 5 / 9} #

#add argument
f_to_celsius <- function(temp_F) {
  temp_C <- (temp_F - 32) * 5 / 9
}

#add return statement
f_to_celsius <- function(temp_F) {
  temp_C <- (temp_F - 32) * 5 / 9
  return(temp_C)
}

```

```{r}
#Test it 
f_to_celsius(32)
```

```{r}
#Test it
f_to_celsius(212)
```

```{r}
#temp_K <- (temp_C + 273.15)

c_to_kelvin <- function(temp_C) { #
  temp_K <- (temp_C + 273.15)
  return(temp_K)}

c_to_kelvin(200)
```

```{r}
library(palmerpenguins)
library(PNWColors)

pal <- pnw_palette("Lake",3,type = "discrete")

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = body_mass_g, y = bill_length_mm, color = island)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  scale_color_manual("Island", values = pal) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
#things to change - make them broad
#arguments to change is always x and y 
#maybe the dataframe 
#maybe even the color

myplot <- function() {
  pal <- pnw_palette("Lake", 3, type = "discrete")
  
  ggplot(penguins, aes(x = body_mass_g, y = bill_length_mm, color = island)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    scale_color_manual("Island", values = pal) +
    theme_bw()
}
```

```{r}
#make it broad

myplot <- function(data, x, y) {
  pal <- pnw_palette("Lake", 3, type = "discrete")
  
  ggplot(penguins, aes(x = x, y = y, color = island)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    scale_color_manual("Island", values = pal) +
    theme_bw()
}

```

```{r}
myplot(data = penguins, x = body_mass_g, y = bill_length_mm)
```
```{r}
#using the curly curly {{}} to pass columns
myplot <- function(data, x, y) {
  pal <- pnw_palette("Lake", 3, type = "discrete")
  
  ggplot(data, aes(x = {{x}}, y = {{y}}, color = island)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    scale_color_manual("Island", values = pal) +
    theme_bw()
}

myplot(data = penguins, x = body_mass_g, y = bill_length_mm)

```
```{r}
myplot(data = penguins, x = body_mass_g, y = flipper_length_mm)
```


```{r}
#set defaults so users dont have to specify everything 
#anytime to change dataframe to be specific 

myplot <- function(data = penguins, x, y) {
  pal <- pnw_palette("Lake", 3, type = "discrete")
  
  ggplot(data, aes(x = {{x}}, y = {{y}}, color = island)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    scale_color_manual("Island", values = pal) +
    theme_bw()
}

#now just only call for the column arguments
myplot(x = body_mass_g, y = flipper_length_mm)
```
```{r}
#can add ggplot layers using the "+" just like regular plot

myplot(x = body_mass_g, y = flipper_length_mm) +
  labs(x = "Body mass (g)", y = "Flipper length (mm)")
```
```{r}
#make functions even. ore broad to give users idea to try out something else
#if-else - use this to execute different code based on condition 

a <- 4
b <- 5

if (a > b) {
  f <- 20
} else {
  f <- 10
}

f #condition (a > b) is FALSE so f is assigneed to 10
#if something is true, then add a line if not, do not add


```
```{r}
#make fxn more flexible

myplot <- function(data = penguins, x, y, lines = TRUE) {
  pal <- pnw_palette("Lake", 3, type = "discrete")
  
  if (lines == TRUE) {
    ggplot(data, aes(x = {{x}}, y = {{y}}, color = island)) +
      geom_point() +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
      scale_color_manual("Island", values = pal) +
      theme_bw()
  } else {
    ggplot(data, aes(x = {{x}}, y = {{y}}, color = island)) +
      geom_point() +
      scale_color_manual("Island", values = pal) +
      theme_bw()
  }
}

#test with lines 
#lines are defaulted to TRUE 
myplot(x = body_mass_g, y = flipper_length_mm)
```
```{r}
#test with no lines
myplot(x = body_mass_g, y = flipper_length_mm, lines = FALSE)
```
